rationale: validation_report and analyzer both flag uncovered_requirement for FR4 and SR1 with mutation_score=0.75 (below acceptable discrimination even though it clears the 0.5 floor, and analyzer_status=fail plus validation_status=fail per the retain rule). Examining the actual mutant files: mutant_SR1_domain_specific_01 genuinely reintroduces the vulnerability by changing the destination bounds check from 64-bit widened arithmetic to 32-bit unsigned arithmetic (uint32_t dst_off, len, dst_end = dst_off + len), which is exactly the CWE-190/CWE-787 wraparound flaw SR1 is meant to catch (offsets[i]=0xFFFFFFF0, lengths[i]=0x20 would wrap in 32-bit but not in 64-bit) -- yet the SR1 check did not fail against it. mutant_FR4_condition_negation_01 genuinely changes the desc_count==0 early-return guard from 'if (desc_count != 0) return 0' -- inverted from the golden's 'if (desc_count == 0) return 0' -- which for desc_count==0 now skips the early return and falls into the kMaxDescriptors check and loops (which happen to still execute zero iterations harmlessly for desc_count==0, but only by chance since the loops are bounded by desc_count itself); this is a real behavioral corruption of the FR4 contract path even if in this particular case desc_count==0 still returns 0 eventually via the loop bounds -- the check should still be strengthened to observe intermediate state or return-code-path deviations. Both mutants are legitimate corruptions of observable behavior, not defective/equivalent mutants, so the fix belongs in evaluation_framework, not mutants.
revision_instructions: Strengthen the SR1 and FR4 checks in evaluate.py so they detect the described corruptions behaviorally through the pinned scatter_gather_copy interface, without relying on source-text inspection. For SR1: add or adjust a test vector that forces a 32-bit-vs-64-bit-arithmetic divergence more robustly -- e.g. supply multiple overflow-adjacent descriptor combinations (vary the wrap magnitude, e.g. offsets[i]=0xFFFFFFFF with lengths[i]=1, and offsets[i]=0x100000000-ish boundary cases expressed as valid 32-bit inputs) so that any implementation performing the destination bounds sum in 32-bit precision will accept at least one crafted out-of-bounds descriptor as valid; assert via a canary buffer placed immediately after dst that it remains unmodified and that the return code is nonzero for every crafted vector, and fail the check if any single wraparound-shaped vector is incorrectly accepted. For FR4: strengthen the desc_count=0 probe so that it does not merely check the final return code and lack of dst writes, but also verifies the function does not depend on offsets/lengths being non-null and does not fall through into any code path that reads them -- e.g. call it with offsets and lengths set to obviously invalid/poisoned non-null pointers pointing at freed or guard memory as well as with null pointers, across repeated calls, and confirm the return code is always exactly 0 and dst is untouched in every case; this way a control-flow inversion in the desc_count==0 short-circuit that happens to still coincidentally return 0 via loop-bound side effects will be caught if it changes any other observable path. Both checks must FAIL when the corrupted behavior described is present and PASS on any correct implementation of the pinned interface -- grade by executing the compiled submission, not by matching source text.
